questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Always wanted to visit Australia and explore all the beautiful nature as well as meeting new people. It was also important for me to study at an English speaking country that was far away from Denmark.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Wollongong was absolutely amazing. Beautiful university and cheaper to live in than Sydney (and some good surf)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy to find the information needed. Once you are enrolled at UOW and get to use their platform, you get messages and e-mails from the university with the needed information. (SOLSS and Outlook)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university gave out a free tote bag to all the new international students where you could find small pamphlets and handbooks with some nice to know information. (also had a few Aussie snacks)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, found it through the host institutions own platform.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There's a free bus (55A and 55C), that goes in a loop in and around the city. So you're able to get to campus or into town easily!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some of the buildings could definitely need an upgrade regarding the facilities (kitchen, bathroom etc.)

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Was a bit overwhelming getting to know the timetable of the different subjects, since it's so different from Denmark.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You apply for the subjects you find interesting and might want to do and then the university will let you know if you have the prerequisites to undertake those subjects. You then enrol the subjects you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Australians are in general very willing to help. So you could always show up at student central if you had any questions or issues.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Managed to register all the classes I wanted, except the ones that I didn't have prerequisites for (obviously)

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's easy, and if you're having issues, just ask a friend!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were to same level of those in Denmark (in my opinion)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: All lectures were online (because of covid), and there weren't a lot of practical classes as I'm used to in Denmark.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIOL341 - Immunity and infectious disease
CHEM325 - Bioinformatics
PHYS295 - Astronomy
CAVA125 - Introduction to photography

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you want a very very easy subject, do PHYS295. CHEM325 was a very well put together subject if you're interested in bioinformatics/proteins.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travel costs. Spend a lot of money on travelling during the mid-session break since everything is more expensive at the touristy areas of Byron bay, Gold Coast, Cairns etc.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Hard liquor, beer and cigarettes are way more expensive in Australia than Denmark. Stick to the goon (boxed white wine) if you're a cheapskate

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't attend any clubs/sports, but from what I heard they were not bad.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had most sports available, badminton, tennis, football, rugby etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: GO SURFING.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel during the mid-session break. I went to Byron bay, whitsunday islands and cairns! Also do the surf camp at 7 mile beach in the first or second weekend when the semester starts. You'll learn all the basics of how to surf and meet new friends. Do a day trip to Jervis bay.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Honestly a bit hard at first when you're not used to striking up conversations with randoms. Since most Australians you randomly meet are super friendly and extroverted, you'll probably feel a bit intimidated.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do activities and do the small events that your accommodation host regularly (especially in the beginning)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Vegemite and vapes.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pubs, chicken schnittys, chicken salt and just how easy it is to make conversation with anybody!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Buy a car! (or at least a bicycle)
even though there is a free bus going around, you should definitely get a car early on since Wollongong is not a major city with loads of public transport. And you'll be able to do trips and go explore Australia during the weekend!
2. If you're interested in clubs/sports sign up for UOW Pulse
3. Most uni-students in Wollongong go out on Wednesday/Thursday instead of the weekend. So be wise when you're able to put together your classes in your timetable, so you don't have too many early classes on Friday.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read the subject outlines thoroughly, they contain all the information regarding; grading, compulsory exercises/assignments and so on.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting all kinds of amazing people from around the globe! Got a lot of friends and a lot more confidence in travelling by my self.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting from living by myself in my own apartment in Copenhagen to suddenly live with 4 Aussie roommates.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: If you're going to stay at campus east. Beware that the self-catered units are nicer and bigger, but you have to do your own shopping and cooking. Although It's also easier to meet people if you're in the catered units since the cafeteria is the place to be to meeting new friends and plan out activities.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
